checklist_contracts.text: The lint rule error kind string must be exactly `action-pinning`.
The rule checks step-level action `uses:` references for version pinning.
The rule checks job-level reusable workflow `uses:` references for version pinning.
The rule is configured via an `action-pinning` config section.
The config section has a `level` field.
The `level` field accepts the value `major-minor`.
The `level` field accepts the value `semver`.
The `level` field accepts the value `commit-sha`.
Level `major-minor` requires vMAJOR.MINOR format.
Level `semver` requires vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH format including prerelease.
Level `commit-sha` requires full 40-character lowercase hex SHA.
The default level when none is specified is `semver`.
The levels are ordered by increasing strictness: a ref satisfying a stricter level also satisfies any less strict requirement.
Setting `action-pinning: null` keeps the rule disabled.
Setting `action-pinning: {}` enables the rule with defaults.
Local refs starting with `./` are skipped (not flagged).

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: a Request body read (e.g., text(), json(), arrayBuffer(), blob()) is in-flight and not yet settled when the shutdown trigger fires
checklist_contracts.text: When shutdown occurs via happyDOM.close(), page.close(), browser.close(), or a navigation that swaps out the active page state, any in-progress Request body read must reject with a DOMException whose name property is "AbortError".

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: a Response body read (e.g., text(), json(), arrayBuffer(), blob()) is in-flight and not yet settled when the shutdown trigger fires
checklist_contracts.text: When shutdown occurs via happyDOM.close(), page.close(), browser.close(), or a navigation that swaps out the active page state, any in-progress Response body read must reject with a DOMException whose name property is "AbortError".

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: multipart formData() parsing is in progress (body consumption and MIME parsing underway) when the shutdown trigger fires
checklist_contracts.text: When shutdown occurs via happyDOM.close(), page.close(), browser.close(), or a navigation that swaps out the active page state, in-progress multipart formData() parsing (reading and parsing multipart body content) must reject with a DOMException whose name property is "AbortError".

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: the read finishes (promise resolves) before any shutdown trigger (happyDOM.close, page.close, browser.close, navigation) fires
checklist_contracts.text: Request and Response body reads that complete successfully before any shutdown trigger fires must remain unchanged — they must resolve normally with their intended value.

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: the Response body's underlying data has been fully loaded into internal buffers before the shutdown trigger fires
checklist_contracts.text: Response bodies whose content has been fully buffered (all payload data loaded into internal buffers) before shutdown must remain readable after shutdown occurs.

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: one or more setTimeout or setInterval callbacks are pending/scheduled on the discarded page state at the time the shutdown or navigation trigger fires

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: Verification requires passing two entries with distinct keys and distinct trait/relation values, then retrieving each by its key to confirm the correct pairing. Using the same value for both entries or the same key proves nothing about position.
checklist_contracts.text: `createTraitRegistry` when passed entries with keys `["a", traitA]` and `["b", traitB]` maps key `"a"` to `traitA` and key `"b"` to `traitB` — each tuple's first element pairs with its second element at construction.
`snapshotEntity(world, entity, registry)` has exactly three parameters in this order: world, entity, registry.
`snapshotEntity` returns an `EntitySnapshot` with shape `{ id: number, traits: Record<string, object | true>, relations?: Record<string, Array<{ targetId: number, data?: object }>> }`.

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: Entity has at least one trait whose value is a mere presence indicator with no data payload.
checklist_contracts.text: In the `EntitySnapshot`, tag traits (traits with no data) are stored as `true` in the `traits` record.

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: Entity has at least one trait whose data contains nested objects or arrays.
checklist_contracts.text: In the `EntitySnapshot`, data traits are stored as a deep copy of the original trait data in the `traits` record.

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: Entity has at least one relation whose store contains nested objects or arrays.
checklist_contracts.text: In the `EntitySnapshot`, relations with a store include `data` as a deep copy of the original relation data.

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: Entity has zero relations.
checklist_contracts.text: In the `EntitySnapshot`, the `relations` property is omitted entirely (not present as a key on the object) when the entity has no relations.

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: entity.isDestroyed() returns true or entity is in a destroyed state.

checklist_contracts.text: If the live cache has newer data (higher data freshness timestamp) but the persisted snapshot has newer error metadata (higher error freshness timestamp), the restored query must keep the newer data while also adopting the newer error state so the result remains a refetch error.

checklist_contracts.text: Restoring over an existing query must merge data freshness and error freshness independently instead of replacing the whole query state as a single unit.

checklist_contracts.text: Pipe query statements use `|>` operators to chain transformations instead of nested clauses.
Pipe queries start with a standalone `FROM` clause (no preceding SELECT or WITH).
Each subsequent `|>` step occupies its own line at base indentation.
The pipe operator `|>` and its clause keyword share the same line.
The clause body starts on the next line after the pipe operator and clause keyword, indented one level deeper.

checklist_contracts.adverse_condition: When the clause type is one that the existing formatter treats as an indented clause (WHERE, SELECT, ORDER BY, AGGREGATE, EXTEND, SET, DROP).
checklist_contracts.text: Clause body indentation follows the same indentation pattern the formatter already uses for that clause type in traditional queries.
Clauses that the existing formatter treats as indented clauses (`WHERE`, `SELECT`, `ORDER BY`, `AGGREGATE`, `EXTEND`, `SET`, `DROP`) place their body on a new indented line after the keyword.
Clauses that the existing formatter treats as one-line clauses (`LIMIT`, `JOIN` and its variants, `AS`) keep their content on the same line as the keyword.
`AGGREGATE` in a pipe step has an optional nested `GROUP BY` sub-clause requiring its own indentation level.
`EXTEND` is a pipe-exclusive clause for computed columns.
`SET` is a pipe-exclusive clause for replacing values.
`DROP` is a pipe-exclusive clause for removing columns.
`AS` is a pipe-exclusive clause for naming intermediates.
Pipe queries enclosed in parentheses are formatted as nested subqueries.
Traditional BigQuery formatting remains unchanged when format is applied to non-pipe queries.
`keywordCase` setting governs all pipe keywords including pipe-exclusive ones (`AGGREGATE`, `EXTEND`, `SET`, `DROP`, `AS`, `GROUP BY` within AGGREGATE).
`|>` must tokenize as a distinct token type, not as bitwise `|` followed by `>`.
Pipe clauses produce structured parse nodes distinct from traditional query parse nodes.
`AGGREGATE` and `EXTEND` are promoted to reserved clauses when they appear after `|>`.
